subject: Standard-decimal arithmetic
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167), CORRECTED THE SAME DAY (kb/Work PB266). r3: 'When operand-2 is less than zero, the result shall be equivalent to the evaluation of the arithmetic expression (1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))' (cite.py --check verified, both halves). This is an EQUIVALENCE and not implementor latitude - r2's latitude is scoped 'When the value of operand-2 is greater than zero' - and under Sec.8.8.1.5.2's per-operation 34-digit rounding the reciprocal form is a DIFFERENT value from exp(-|p| x ln b): it carries one extra correctly-rounded division and no negated exp argument. ⛔ THE FIRST LANDING'S NOTE CLAIMED THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE CODE DID, in both of its sentences. It said the development 'develops every other negative exponent through the same SDIDI exp/ln core as the positive one, so the r3 identity holds by construction rather than by luck'; measured, it held in 21% of sampled cases, BY LUCK (2 ** -0.25 answered ...4762332146 where 1 / (2 ** 0.25) is ...4762332141). It also said 'the INTEGER arm has honoured it whole since PB145'; the past-loop-bound escape carried the sign INSIDE the exponent, so r3 held below |n| = 500000 and broke above it - a discontinuity at the loop bound. And no pin on the row could see either: pb167's two negative legs and MinusHalfExponent were all -1/2 (the one exponent PowCore short-circuited), pb145's B ** NN and MinusOne_...PastLongRange are base -1 (the |b| = 1 parity shortcut), and HalfPastTheLoopBound uses a POSITIVE exponent. THE CONSTRUCTION NOW: r3's reciprocal is written ONCE, at the top of Pow, over PowMagnitude(b, |operand-2|) - so every arm below it is r3-correct by construction, PowCore needs no -1/2 twin to keep in step, and the divergence is closed at the 34th significant digit where a relation between two SDIDI intermediates and an exact cancellation could both see it (pb167's R3GEN / R3PW7 / R3FAR / R3NEAR / R3DLT legs, and a 10-row unit theory spanning the non-integer, in-bound-integer and past-bound arms). ⚠ ONE VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, pinned: an out-of-range negative exponent now takes its EC name from r3's own expression rather than from where the final value lands, because the operation that leaves the range is the INNER power. 2 ** -600000 reports EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and 0.5 ** -600000 EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW; before the hoist they answered the other way round (pb145's R3OVER / R3UNDR legs). ⚠ r3 is an IDENTITY requirement, not an accuracy one, and honouring it COSTS accuracy here: the true 34-digit 2**-0.25 is ...4762332149, so the reciprocal form is 8 ulp out where the direct form was 3. That is why the fix is the literal expression and never a tolerance.
